n: Spot it: Three fused bones: ilium, ischium and pubis. The two coxal bones meet in front and join the sacrum in back.
Tell sides: Put the pubic symphysis in front and the acetabulum facing out.
Spot it: The hip socket the head of the femur fits into. You can see where the three bones fuse inside it.
Don't confuse: The obturator foramen is the big hole below it, not a socket.
Spot it: The lower of the two front bumps on the ilium, just above the acetabulum.
Don't confuse: The anterior superior iliac spine is higher, where the iliac crest ends in front.
Spot it: The front end of the iliac crest.
Don't confuse: The anterior inferior iliac spine is the smaller bump just below it.
Spot it: The rough patch on the inner back of the ilium where the coxal bone joins the sacrum.
Don't confuse: The sacrum has its own auricular surface that matches this one.
Spot it: The big notch on the back edge where the sciatic nerve leaves the pelvis. Your hand sits here when you hold the bone like a phone.
Don't confuse: The lesser sciatic notch is the small divot below the ischial spine.
Spot it: The curved top rim of the ilium, from the front spine to the back spine.
Spot it: The large, concave surface on the inside of the ilium.
Spot it: The largest of the three coxal bones, forming the top of the hip.
Spot it: The lower border of the pubis, running down to meet the ischial ramus.
Don't confuse: The superior pubic ramus forms the top edge of the obturator foramen.
Spot it: Just in front of the ischial tuberosity, where the ischium joins the pubis.
Don't confuse: The inferior pubic ramus is the pubis side of that same bar.
Spot it: A pointed projection on the back of the ischium, between the two sciatic notches.
Don't confuse: The ischial tuberosity is the big rough lump below it.
Spot it: The part you sit on. Back-of-thigh muscles attach here.
Don't confuse: The ischial spine is the sharp point above it.
Spot it: The back, lower part of the coxal bone.
Spot it: A small divot below the ischial spine where nerves and vessels pass.
Don't confuse: The greater sciatic notch is much bigger and sits above the ischial spine.
Spot it: The large hole in the lower coxal bone, framed by the pubis and ischium. Soft tissue covers it in life.
Spot it: The lower of the two back bumps, just above the greater sciatic notch. It anchors ligaments for the joint with the sacrum.
Don't confuse: The posterior superior iliac spine is higher, where the iliac crest ends in back.
Spot it: The back end of the iliac crest.
Don't confuse: The posterior inferior iliac spine is the bump just below it.
Spot it: The top front edge of the pubis, where abdominal muscles attach.
Spot it: The front, lower part of the coxal bone.
Spot it: Forms the upper edge of the obturator foramen.
Don't confuse: The inferior pubic ramus forms the lower edge.
Spot it: Where the two coxal bones meet in front.
Spot it: The largest, heaviest and strongest bone in the body.
Tell sides: The shallow groove between the condyles faces front.
Spot it: The long, round shaft in the middle of the bone.
Spot it: A small pit in the head of the femur, where a ligament ties it to the acetabulum.
Spot it: The lateral ridge near the top of the back of the shaft, where the gluteus maximus attaches.
Don't confuse: The linea aspera is the long ridge running down the middle of the back.
Spot it: The big knob on the outer top of the femur. It makes the widest part of the hip.
Don't confuse: The lesser trochanter is the smaller knob on the inner back side.
Spot it: The ball at the top that fits into the acetabulum.
Spot it: The deep notch on the back between the two condyles.
Don't confuse: The patellar groove is the shallow groove on the front.
Spot it: A ridge on the back of the femur running between the greater and lesser trochanters.
Spot it: The smooth outer knuckle at the bottom that meets the tibia.
Don't confuse: The lateral epicondyle is the rough bump just above it.
Spot it: The rough bump just above the lateral condyle, where ligaments attach.
Don't confuse: The lateral condyle is the smooth surface below it that touches the tibia.
Spot it: The smaller knob on the inner back side, below the neck.
Don't confuse: The greater trochanter is the big knob on the outer top.
Spot it: The long ridge down the back of the shaft, where muscles attach.
Don't confuse: The gluteal tuberosity is the branch of it near the top on the outer side.
Spot it: The smooth inner knuckle at the bottom that meets the tibia.
Don't confuse: The medial epicondyle is the rough bump just above it.
Spot it: The rough bump just above the medial condyle, where ligaments attach.
Don't confuse: The medial condyle is the smooth surface below it that touches the tibia.
Spot it: The part between the head and the trochanters.
Spot it: The shallow groove on the front between the condyles, where the patella glides.
Don't confuse: The intercondylar fossa is the deep notch on the back.
Spot it: The kneecap.
Tell sides: Look at the back with the apex down; the bigger facet is lateral.
Spot it: The front of the kneecap, the part you can feel through your skin.
Spot it: The pointed bottom of the kneecap.
Don't confuse: The base is the broad top.
Spot it: The broad top of the kneecap.
Don't confuse: The apex is the pointed bottom.
Spot it: The back of the kneecap, with two facets that glide on the femur.
Spot it: The larger of the two back facets. It meets the lateral condyle of the femur.
Don't confuse: The medial facet is the smaller one.
Spot it: The smaller of the two back facets. It meets the medial condyle of the femur.
Don't confuse: The lateral facet is the larger one.
Spot it: The bigger lower-leg bone, always on the medial side. It carries most of the weight.
Tell sides: Face the tibial tuberosity forward; the medial malleolus is on the inner side.
Spot it: The sharp ridge down the front of the tibia: your shin.
Spot it: The notch on the lower outer tibia where the fibula fits.
Spot it: The two-pointed ridge on top of the tibia between the two condyle surfaces. Knee ligaments attach here.
Spot it: The outer top surface of the tibia, which meets the lateral condyle of the femur.
Spot it: The inner top surface of the tibia, which meets the medial condyle of the femur.
Spot it: The bump on the inside of your ankle, at the bottom of the tibia.
Don't confuse: The lateral malleolus is the outer ankle bump, on the fibula.
Spot it: The bump on the front of the tibia just below the patella.
Spot it: The thin lower-leg bone, always lateral to the tibia.
Spot it: The top knob of the fibula. It touches the tibia but not the femur.
Spot it: The bump on the outside of your ankle, at the bottom of the fibula.
Don't confuse: The medial malleolus is the inner ankle bump, on the tibia.
Spot it: Sits under the tibia and fibula and forms the ankle joint with them.
Tip: Tarsals in order: Thin Country Nerds Meet Incredible Lovely Cuties (talus, calcaneus, navicular, cuneiforms, cuboid).
Spot it: The heel bone, the largest and strongest bone in the foot. Calf muscles attach here.
Spot it: Boat-shaped, on the inner side of the foot in front of the talus.
Spot it: The innermost of the three wedge-shaped cuneiforms.
Spot it: The middle wedge, just lateral to the medial cuneiform.
Spot it: The outermost of the three wedges, next to the cuboid.
Spot it: Cube-shaped, on the outer side of the foot in front of the calcaneus.
Spot it: The five long bones between the tarsals and the toes.
Spot it: The metatarsal under the big toe.
Spot it: Two pea-shaped bones in the ball of the foot under the big-toe joint. They act as a pulley for tendons.
Don't confuse: They are not tarsals.
Spot it: The metatarsal under the second toe, next to the big toe.
Spot it: The metatarsal under the middle toe.
Spot it: The metatarsal under the fourth toe.
Spot it: The metatarsal under the little toe.
Spot it: The toe bones. The four small toes have distal, middle and proximal phalanges; the big toe has no middle one.
Spot it: The tip bone of each toe.
Spot it: The middle bone of the four small toes. The big toe has none.
Spot it: The toe bone closest to the metatarsals.
